subject.title: Feature request: Auto-send intent/acknowledgment text message before agent processing

question: Should OpenClaw solve this as a global messages.ackText-style config, a generic non-terminal plugin/channel hook, or only channel-specific placeholder features?
rationale: The source-level gap is real, but the permanent boundary affects core config, plugin API, and per-channel UX contracts.

options.title: Define a generic acknowledgement hook
options.body: Add a default-off send-and-continue lifecycle contract first, then expose config/docs where the contract proves it belongs.

options.title: Add global messages.ackText
options.body: Ship the reporter's requested config shape directly, accepting a new core config surface that every channel must interpret consistently.

options.title: Keep this channel-specific
options.body: Let Slack, Telegram, Discord, Feishu, and other plugins implement their own placeholders without a cross-channel core contract.

recommendation.title: Define a generic acknowledgement hook
recommendation.body: Add a default-off send-and-continue lifecycle contract first, then expose config/docs where the contract proves it belongs.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter is the strongest current-history routing candidate for the config, dispatch, and reply-lifecycle boundary involved here.
